item.title: Artifacts
item.description:
Loom publishes JVM artifacts, a command line client and container deployment assets separately.

Maven Artifacts

See Maven Artifacts for the BOM and the primary client and shared model modules.

item.title: Authentication
item.description: Loom uses JWT (JSON Web Token) bearer tokens for API authentication. OAuth2 integration is also available.

item.title: Binary Storage
item.description: Every asset in Loom has two halves: the record — filename, hashes, tags, everything a pipeline worked out about it — and the bytes themselves. This page is about the bytes: where they go, how you put them there, and how you get them back.

item.title: Chat & AI Agent
item.description: Loom ships with a built-in AI assistant — an OpenAI-style chat, backed by a server-side agentic loop that runs inside the Loom backend. Users converse with their asset domain in natural language ("find beach videos", "what tasks are open for me?", "summarize this clip’s transcript") and the agent answers by calling Loom’s own tools with the caller’s permissions.

item.title: Containers
item.description: The Loom server is distributed as the metaloom/loom-server image (JVM and -native variants). For a zero-config first run, use the all-in-one metaloom/loom-demo image instead — see Getting Started. The full image list is on Container Images.

item.title: Database Integrity
item.description: Loom keeps a catalogue: assets and the things said about them — tags, people, transcripts, tasks, comments, pipeline runs. Most of the rules that keep it coherent are enforced by the database itself, which simply refuses anything that would break them. A handful cannot be, and this page is about those.

item.title: Examples
item.description:
The /examples directory of the source repository contains runnable example projects.

Listing Examples

The examples/ Maven module contains sub-projects for both Loom and Cortex use cases.

item.title: Features
item.description: Loom provides a comprehensive set of features for managing digital media assets and their associated metadata. Each section below links to the reference page that covers the feature in depth.

item.title: GraphQL API
item.description: Loom exposes a GraphQL API for flexible, nested queries over the asset data model — fetch an asset together with its components and locations in a single request, selecting exactly the fields you need.

item.title: Helm Chart
item.description: Kubernetes is the supported production deployment path for Loom. There are two Helm charts in the source repository — helm/loom for the server and helm/cortex for the workers.

item.title: Java Client Usage
item.description:
The loom-client-rest module provides a typed HTTP client for JVM applications.

Maven Dependency

<dependency>
    <groupId>io.metaloom.loom.client</groupId>
    <artifactId>loom-client-rest</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
</dependency>

item.title: Metrics
item.description: The Loom server exposes a Prometheus scrape endpoint at GET /metrics on a dedicated monitoring port. All Loom meters are prefixed loom_. For Cortex worker metrics see Cortex Metrics; for health and readiness endpoints see Monitoring API.

item.title: Python Client Usage
item.description: The Python client is a synchronous binding for the Loom REST API. It is built entirely on the Python standard library and has no third-party dependencies, so it drops into a processing script or a container without pulling anything else in.

item.title: REST API
item.description: Loom exposes its full functionality via a versioned REST API. All endpoints are rooted at /api/v1.

item.title: Search Indices
item.description: Loom keeps several indices so that searching, face matching and duplicate detection are fast. They are maintained automatically and you can normally ignore them. This page is for the times you cannot: after a bulk import, after changing an embedding model, or when search is returning less than you expect.
